title: 988 can improve crisis-line operations without producing a detectable short-run mortality change
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35601, difference-in-differences evaluation of the July 2022 988 implementation
geography: United States states with differing pre-988 crisis-line capacity gaps and national suicide-mortality and mental-health outcomes

observations.period: July 2022 988 rollout and post-implementation short-run period

denominator.unit: U.S. states and population outcomes in the study's cross-state panel; exact public abstract denominator not disclosed

crisis_line_operations.value: states with larger pre-988 capacity gaps answered more calls in-state and increased their in-state answer rates

suicide_mortality.value: no detectable short-run reduction; estimates are precise enough to rule out even modest reductions

broader_mental_health.value: no statistically significant improvement in broader population mental-health outcomes

downstream_crisis_care.value: not observed in the public abstract
downstream_crisis_care.unit: missing caller-level connection to counseling, emergency dispatch, treatment, safety planning, repeat contact, and longer-run recovery

observations.method: Difference-in-differences design using pre-existing cross-state variation in crisis-line capacity gaps, measured by pre-988 calls routed to a state but not answered in-state; operational, mortality, and broader mental-health endpoints are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public abstract does not disclose exact state and observation counts, the complete post-implementation horizon, subgroup effects, or the full crisis-care pathway. A population-level mortality null does not show that no caller benefited or that later effects cannot emerge.
observations.subgroup: States differentiated by baseline crisis-line capacity gaps; callers, age groups, race, gender, firearm access, local crisis systems, and people receiving follow-up care are not linked in the abstract.
observations.counterinterpretation: 988 may improve access, connection, or immediate safety for some people without moving short-run population mortality. Mortality may require downstream treatment, housing, social support, means safety, or repeated care that a hotline alone cannot provide.

boundary: This record measures an operational gain from 988 implementation and null short-run population outcomes for suicide mortality and broader mental health. It does not establish no individual benefit, no change in crisis access, or a complete test of the downstream care and social-support system.
